item.title: How to Check If a Website Is Safe Before You Trust It
item.description: Before you enter a password or card on a website, run these quick checks: the exact domain, the connection, the age and reputation of the site, and its contact details. Here is the full checklist.

item.title: Voice Cloning Scams: The Fake Family Emergency Call
item.description: Scammers can clone a loved one's voice from seconds of audio and call you in a panic asking for money. Learn how the fake emergency call works, the signs, and the family code word that stops it.

item.title: What Is a UPI Scam? How UPI Fraud Works and How to Stay Safe
item.description: A UPI scam tricks you into approving a payment you think is a refund or a receipt. Learn the common UPI frauds, the one rule that stops most of them, and what to do if you were tricked.

item.title: What Is Phishing? How to Spot and Avoid It
item.description: Phishing is when scammers impersonate a trusted brand or person to trick you into handing over passwords, OTPs, or money. Learn the common types, the warning signs, and exactly what to do.

item.title: What Is Smishing? SMS and Text Scams Explained
item.description: Smishing is phishing over text messages: fake delivery fees, bank alerts, and prize links designed to steal your details or money. Learn the signs and what to do about a suspicious SMS.

item.title: What Is Vishing? Voice Call Scams Explained
item.description: Vishing is phishing over a phone call: a fake official, bank agent, or support desk pressuring you to share codes or move money. Learn how it works and how to shut it down.

item.title: Can ChatGPT Tell If a Message Is a Scam? What It Can and Can't Check
item.description: ChatGPT can recognize scam patterns in text you paste, but it can't open links, verify senders, check breach databases, or watch for follow-ups. Here's where a chatbot helps, where it fails, and what to use instead.

item.title: Kaval vs Truecaller: What Each One Actually Protects You From
item.description: Truecaller tells you who is calling. Kaval tells you whether the message, link, or forward itself is a scam. Here's what each covers, where they overlap, and why many people use both.
